verses.text: In the days when the judges led Israel, there was a famine in the land. So a man from Bethlehem in Judah went with his wife and two sons to live for a while in the country of Moab.
The man's name was Elimelek, his wife's name was Naomi, and his two sons were named Mahlon and Kilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They went to Moab and lived there.
Then Elimelek, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
They married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other Ruth. After they had lived there about ten years,
both Mahlon and Kilion also died. Naomi was left alone, without her two sons and her husband.
While she was in Moab, Naomi heard that the LORD had come to help his people by giving them food again. So she and her daughters-in-law got ready to go back home from Moab.
With her two daughters-in-law she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road that would take them back to the land of Judah.
Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's home. May the LORD be kind to you, as you have been kind to your dead husbands and to me.
May the LORD give each of you rest in the home of a new husband." Then she kissed them goodbye, and they cried loudly
and said to her, "No! We will go back with you to your people."
But Naomi said, "Go home, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Am I going to have any more sons who could become your husbands?
Go home, my daughters. I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was still hope for me, even if I had a husband tonight and then gave birth to sons,
would you wait until they grew up? Would you stay unmarried for them? No, my daughters. My life is much more bitter than yours, because the LORD's hand has turned against me!"
At this they cried loudly again. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
"Look," said Naomi, "your sister-in-law is going back to her people and her gods. Go back with her."
But Ruth replied, "Do not ask me to leave you or to turn back from you. Where you go, I will go, and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD punish me severely if anything but death separates you and me."
When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
So the two women went on until they came to Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was stirred up because of them. The women said, "Can this be Naomi?"
"Do not call me Naomi, which means Pleasant," she told them. "Call me Mara, which means Bitter, because the Almighty has made my life very bitter.
I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? The LORD has spoken against me. The Almighty has brought trouble on me."
So Naomi came back from Moab with Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law. They arrived in Bethlehem as the barley harvest was beginning.
